article.title: Common mistake: 'explain me' vs 'explain to me'
article.description: Wrong: 'Can you explain me this?' Right: 'Can you explain this to me?' Teaching point: 'explain' takes the thing being explained as its direct object, and the person needs 'to' before them — unlike 'tell me' which doesn't need 'to'.
article.content: Wrong: 'Can you explain me this?' Right: 'Can you explain this to me?' Teaching point: 'explain' takes the thing being explained as its direct object, and the person needs 'to' before them — unlike 'tell me' which doesn't need 'to'.

generated.caption:
Ever wondered if you should say "explain me" or "explain to me"? 🤔 The word 'explain' needs *what* you're explaining directly. The person comes after 'to'!

So, instead of 'Can you explain me this?', say:
✅ Can you explain this to me?

generated.script: Ye 'explain me' aur 'explain to me'? Isme bahut log galti karte hain! Kya aapko pata hai 'explain me' galat hai? Dekho, 'explain' word ke baad, woh cheez aati hai jo aap explain kar rahe ho – as a direct object. Aur jis *person* ko explain kar rahe ho na, uske pehle 'to' lagta hai. Jaise hum 'tell me' bolte hain directly, vaise 'explain' ke saath nahi hota. Example: 'Can you explain this to me?' Ye right hai. Toh next time remember, it's always 'explain something *to* someone'. slides.body: It's a common slip-up, but saying 'explain me' is grammatically incorrect. The verb 'explain' requires the thing being explained to be its direct object, and the person receiving the explanation needs the preposition 'to' before them. For example, instead of 'Can you explain me this?', the correct phrasing is 'Can you explain this to me?' This differs from verbs like 'tell', where you can directly say 'tell me something' without 'to'.
